methodology: Walk-forward historical backtest: for each real consecutive season pair (T, T+1), predict T+1's real rate using only evidence through T, evaluated with weighted MAE (weighted by real T+1 sample size). Grid search over lambda in [0.40,0.95] and attribute-specific M grids, refined with a finer/lower M pass after the coarse grid showed several attributes preferred M near the grid floor. Selected by minimum weighted MAE across ALL walk-forward pairs (NOT a separate held-out subset of those pairs -- see KNOWN_LIMITATIONS in player_ability_calibration.py).

passing.note: Real, large finding: provisional M=1500 was WAY too high -- even NO shrinkage (Baseline C) beat the old provisional system. True optimum needs much less shrinkage than assumed.

offensive_rebounding.note: Largest improvement found (32.7% vs provisional B). Same over-shrinkage problem as passing.

defensive_playmaking.note: Smallest relative improvement (8.3%) of the six. Real age-residual bias found (see report) that this simple lambda/M model cannot fix -- flagged for a future age-aware model, not addressed here.

not_calibrated.ball_security: Explicitly excluded per this phase's scope -- the production estimator still uses the old total-TOV proxy, not the (unintegrated) turnover-subtype prototype.
